candidate.title: CLASH
candidate.scope: The CLASH (Crosslinking, ligation, and sequencing of hybrids) row in the assigned Illumina poster crop: a single schematic route from a protein-associated RNA duplex through UV crosslinking, affinity purification, end ligation and reverse transcription to cDNA. A/B are generic RNA partners, not a specified miRNA-only implementation. The matching collection page has the CLASH heading and the same diagram. Neighboring miTRAP, scRNA-seq, partial DLAF and chemical-structure panels are catalogue context, not alternatives to CLASH. No branches or pooling are depicted. The poster overview icon is descriptive, not a second input route. This is a schematic-level architecture, not a complete library-preparation recipe or an assertion that all CLASH implementations are identical.

operations.label: UV crosslinking
operations.description: UV treatment converts the depicted protein-associated RNA duplex into the crosslinked complex while retaining RNAs A and B with the protein.
operations.mechanism: The catalogue identifies UV crosslinking of RNA–protein complexes. The diagram supplies a UV lightning symbol, without specifying a bond structure or a separate RNA–RNA crosslinking reagent.
operations.information_effect: Stabilizes the protein-associated RNA pair for subsequent capture; it does not yet encode the pair as a joined sequence.

operations.label: Affinity purification
operations.description: Affinity purification selects the crosslinked RNA–protein complex for the subsequent ligation step. Its output retains the crosslinked protein association and both RNA segments.
operations.mechanism: Protein-directed affinity selection is shown as a single broad operation; the affinity reagent and bait identity are unspecified.
operations.information_effect: Restricts the sampled RNA interactions to the captured protein-associated complexes. The selected material is an enriched population, not evidence that all cellular RNA duplexes were sampled.

operations.description: The ends of RNAs A and B in the purified complex are joined to produce the looped A–B RNA hybrid shown on the protein.

operations.label: Reverse transcription

method_scopes.rationale: The card title, expanded name on the CLASH row, and matching collection-page caption identify CLASH alone. All four local operations apply to this drawn route. The primary Kudla paper abstract explicitly identifies CLASH and its intra/intermolecular RNA-interaction readout; it is abstract-only evidence here and does not independently verify the detailed reaction order. The diagram and matched secondary description support that order. The paper reports yeast examples, while the diagram leaves bait and RNA identities generic. The collection also lists Helwak et al. (2013) as reference 130; only its secondary bibliographic listing is available in this packet, so it is not treated as inspected primary content or used to assign human-miRNA-specific operations.
